title: Infection-related glomerulonephritis

steps.tx: Classic **Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis** follows **Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus** upper respiratory pharyngitis by a latent period of **1** to **2** weeks. In contrast, cutaneous pyoderma and **impetigo** exhibit an extended latent incubation interval spanning **3** to **6** weeks before nephritic symptoms and macroscopic hematuria manifest.

steps.tx: Circulating cationic streptococcal antigens, predominantly nephritis-associated plasmin receptor (**NAPlr**) and streptococcal pyrogenic exotoxin B (**SPEB**), plant directly within glomerular capillary walls. These planted antigens recruit circulating plasmin and activate the **alternative pathway** of complement, triggering localized endocapillary inflammation and severe microvascular glomerular damage.

steps.tx: Glomerular histology in post-streptococcal disease displays diffuse **endocapillary proliferative** glomerulonephritis marked by prominent neutrophilic infiltration filling capillary lumens. Immunofluorescence demonstrates pathognomonic capillary wall **starry sky** granular C3 deposition, while electron microscopy confirms massive dome-shaped **subepithelial humps** residing beneath the podocyte cytoplasm.

steps.tx: Profound depression of **serum complement C3** occurs in over **90%** of acute PSGN presentations, driven by intense alternative complement consumption. Spontaneous normalization of circulating C3 concentrations typically occurs within **6** to **8** weeks; persistent hypocomplementemia lasting beyond **8** to **12** weeks mandates urgent kidney biopsy to evaluate for **C3 glomerulopathy** or MPGN.

steps.tx: Diagnostic antibody titers against **Anti-streptolysin O** (**ASO**) rise reliably following streptococcal pharyngitis but remain persistently negative in up to 50% of skin infections. Conversely, serum **anti-DNase B** and anti-hyaluronidase titers exhibit superior diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for confirming antecedent streptococcal impetigo and pyoderma.

steps.tx: Infection-related glomerulonephritis triggered by **Staphylococcus aureus** (frequently **MRSA**) predominantly afflicts elderly diabetic adults harboring occult deep-seated visceral **visceral abscesses**, endocarditis, or osteomyelitis. Kidney biopsy characteristically reveals an atypical pattern dominated by prominent mesangial and capillary wall **IgA deposition**, frequently mimicking primary IgA nephropathy.

steps.tx: Valvular **Infective endocarditis** induces immune complex glomerulonephritis marked by prominent **hypocomplementemia** with depressed C3 and C4 concentrations. Circulating **ANCA positivity** (specifically targeting PR3 or MPO) emerges in **20%** to **30%** of bacteremic cases, causing diagnostic confusion with primary systemic vasculitis where immunosuppression proves disastrous.

steps.tx: Chronic ventriculoatrial cerebrospinal fluid shunts colonized by coagulase-negative staphylococci produce classical **Shunt nephritis**. Patients present with persistent low-grade fever, systemic microvascular purpura, hepatosplenomegaly, and **membranoproliferative** glomerulonephritis displaying intense classical complement consumption, which resolves definitively following **surgical removal** of the infected hardware.
